newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas prices mixed, awaiting Nov 1 flows.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas prices mixed, awaiting Nov 1 flows.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices were mixed Thursday as most sources said they were hesitant to trade swing gas before nominated gas begins flowing Friday.
Swing Gulf Coast prices were notionally talked higher in the high-$2.70s, up at least five cents from most index levels, but no deals could be confirmed done.
Market sources attributed the firmness to forecasts for continued cold in the Midwest through the end of the week and the likelihood of below-normal temperatures this weekend in the Northeast.

Despite the strength in the Gulf, a larger number of sellers were offering Midcontinent gas for swing delivery today, particularly on Northern where nominations were still being accepted. As a result, prices were notionally talked lower in the low-to-mid $2.70s.
Forecasters said temperatures were expected to moderate by Sunday in most of the Midwest, thereby weakening heating demand.
In west Texas, prices also eased for one-day deliveries as forecasters anticipated more moderate temperatures this weekend in the West.
Limited volumes of Permian basin gas traded in the high-$2.60s to low-$2.70s, while at the southern California border prices slipped about three cents to the mid-$2.80s.
In the Appalachian region, traders said baseload prices wavered in the $3.10 area, while swing gas for November 1 traded as high as $3.50.
